raw_response:
The raw_customers table contains numeric region codes ('01'-'04') alongside region names. raw_region_map gives an unambiguous mapping from code to name, with one row per code, so the fix is deterministic. The fix is to map the codes with a LEFT JOIN to raw_region_map, falling back to the existing value when no code matches. Regions stay uppercase, and the output columns are unchanged. The map's region_name values are already uppercase, but I apply upper() anyway. Joining on region = region_code only matches the four numeric codes, so existing names fall through to the COALESCE fallback. There are no duplicate rows, because region_code is distinct. Trimming the value is a harmless extra safeguard.
{"diagnosis": "Some customers in raw_customers have numeric region codes (01-04) instead of region names; raw_region_map provides an unambiguous code-to-name mapping, so silver_customers should translate the codes.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.9, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_customers": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_customers AS SELECT c.customer_id, upper(COALESCE(m.region_name, trim(c.region))) AS region FROM raw_customers c LEFT JOIN raw_region_map m ON trim(c.region) = m.region_code"}}
